transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-01
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Rita (Redwood CSM), Lena (Avalon Head of AI), Tom (Avalon Platform Eng), Priya (Avalon CISO), Owen (Avalon SRE), Sofia (Avalon Procurement)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Renewal window in 6 weeks; Avalon wants to lock rates and add EU edge nodes for lower latency in Frankfurt and Paris.
- Primary success criteria: p95 latency < 120ms for 512-token responses during peak events, SOC2/ISO compliance, and predictable cost under burst scenarios.
- Action: Redwood to provide pricing/plan, run benchmarks, and schedule pilot.

[00:00] Maya (AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Lena (Avalon): Yep, Lena here.
[00:07] Tom (Avalon): Tom here.
[00:09] Priya (Avalon): Priya here.
[00:10] Maya: Great. We've got about 50 minutes. High level: we wanted to walk through renewal terms, the EU edge plan you mentioned, and next steps to pilot. Diego will jump into the performance plan in a bit.
[02:12] Diego (SE): Cool. Before we dive, can someone remind me of the target traffic profile for peak sale days? I have an old spreadsheet but want the latest.
[02:25] Tom: Sure - during Black Friday last year we saw short spikes up to 4.8k RPS for the recommendation+personalization endpoints, sustained for about 12 minutes, then a tail. Average daily RPS is ~230.
[02:45] Diego: OK that's helpful. For the EU nodes we usually size for sustained plus 2x burst headroom, but we can tune batching to keep cost low.
[03:12] Lena: Our big ask is p95 latency under 120ms for 512 tokens. We also want data to remain in EU for those routes.
[03:28] Diego: Right, so two options we typically recommend: dedicated capacity in EU (Reserved GPUs) or a private EU VPC deployment. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower p95, private VPC gives you full control over networking. There's a cost and ops tradeoff.
[04:01] Maya: Pricing-wise we can do a blended renewal that includes a reserved capacity commit for EU with burst credits if you want predictable monthly cost. We'll draft that.
[04:32] Sofia (Proc): Important for procurement — we need clear surge pricing and a cap for unexpected events. Last renewal had surprise overages.
[04:45] Maya: Understood. We can add a soft cap alerting threshold and a hard cap option that requires approval before exceeding.
[05:10] Priya (CISO): Also encryption: what's the default for key management in the EU private option? We need KMS with customer-managed keys and HSM backed if possible, plus audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[05:28] Diego: We support KMS integrations, and for Private we can do HSM-backed KMS. Audit logs are available and can be streamed to a customer's S3 or SIEM via remote log shipping. I'll put exact doc links in the follow-up.
[05:45] Priya: And retention windows — can we set short retention for request logs in EU only?
[05:56] Diego: Yes; retention is configurable per-route or per-tenant. We'll share config examples.
[06:15] Owen (SRE): One more ops question: failover. If the EU edge loses capacity, what's the fallback? Do requests hit a multi-region hosted model with higher latency?
[06:29] Rita (CSM): We have automatic fallback policies: try local EU pool, then fallback to nearest compatible model in another region or to lower-precision quantized model. That behavior is configurable by you.
[06:49] Lena: We need deterministic behavior for customer-facing experiences — if fallback happens we want a flag indicating downgraded quality so UX can adapt.
[07:00] Diego: Yep we can add a response header and telemetry tag for quality tier.
[07:12] [crosstalk, unintelligible for a few seconds]
[08:05] Maya: Let's talk numbers. Our draft renewal will propose a 12-month extension with a base reserved commit for NODE-EU-M (equivalent to X GPUs), plus a burst pool. We'll include a chart showing estimated cost at your current RPS and projected Black Friday spike.
[08:40] Tom: Can you include an explicit cost per 1M tokens for streaming vs non-streaming? We want to line-item them.
[08:51] Maya: Yes. We'll break down token pricing, per-request overhead, and queue/prefetch logic.
[09:20] Diego: For performance tests, given your 4.8k RPS spikes, we'll run a 72-hour soak with synthetic traffic plus a Black Friday style spike. We'll instrument KV cache hit rates and batching behavior. Expect separate reports: latency P50/P95/P99 and token cost per 1k.
[10:05] Lena: Good. Also run with our prompts; I'll upload a sanitized sample set to the shared drive after this call.
[10:15] Tom: We'll add and send the tracer logs.
[10:22] [brief pause while link is pasted]
[11:02] Maya: Noted. Diego, can you walk through the suggested hardware for EU dedicated?
[11:10] Diego: For your workload we'd recommend a mix: 2 nodes of A100-80GB equiv for the steady state plus 4x smaller T4-style quantized endpoints for bursty short requests, plus a pooling layer that routes long-context requests to the big nodes. That gets latency down while keeping cost efficient.
[11:46] Tom: Is that multi-tenant or single-tenant?
[11:50] Diego: Dedicated capacity is single-tenant. The T4 quantized paths can be in a shared pool if you prefer cheaper ops; but for predictable latency we recommend making them reserved for you during Black Friday window.
[12:10] Priya: If we do private VPC, who manages OS/patching?
[12:16] Diego: For Private deployments, Redwood can offer a managed ops add-on where we handle infra patching and security updates, or you can self-manage. We'll outline both in the doc.
[12:34] Priya: We'll need the SOC2 & ISO artifacts before sign-off.
[12:40] Maya: We'll attach those and provide a one-pager showing what each cert covers.
[13:05] Sofia (Procurement): Timelines — procurement wants an option to sign a 12-month with a short opt-out window for the first 60 days of the pilot, is that possible?
[13:20] Maya: We can offer a pilot period addendum that allows adjustments after pilot. We typically do 30- to 90-day pilots with a trial commitment clause; we'll propose a 60-day review in the draft.
[13:40] Lena: We also want SLAs: uptime and latency playbook. Can you commit to 99.9% for the dedicated EU pool?
[13:52] Rita: We can commit to SLA targets and have credits for downtime. 99.9% is possible with Dedicated and properly configured autoscale. We'll show exact SLA language.
[14:12] Owen: On telemetry — do you export traces in OpenTelemetry?
[14:17] Diego: Yes, we push span+metrics and you can route them to OTEL-compatible backends. We'll include sample dashboards.
[14:35] [18:00-20:00 omitted small side conversation about calendar slots and internal handoffs]
[20:12] Tom: One thing: during internal load tests we saw that payloads that use multimodal enrichments cause high variance in latency. Any guidance?
[20:26] Diego: For multimodal you should split enrichment stages — do image embedding asynchronously and cache results. We can help with a pipeline pattern that reduces tail latency.
[20:45] Lena: That's helpful. We'll work with SE to instrument that pipeline.
[21:00] Maya: Quick question on decision criteria — what will make Avalon renew vs look at alternatives?
[21:10] Lena: Three things: 1) predictable cost and no surprise overages, 2) demonstrable p95 latency under 120ms for target requests during peak, 3) compliance controls and KMS.
[21:28] Priya: And a clear playbook for failover with flags for degraded responses.
[21:40] Maya: Understood. We'll design the renewal package to hit those boxes.
[22:05] Diego: I'll add instrumentation flags to detect degraded responses and return a quality tag; we'll demo it in the pilot.
[22:25] [background noise, faint keyboard]
[23:10] Sofia: Procurement needs a clear cancellation and renewal window in the contract doc.
[23:20] Maya: We'll include a plain-language summary and a separate contract appendix for procurement.
[24:02] Tom: Benchmarks — can you also measure token cost if we enable prefix KV caching aggressively? That could save a lot for personalization workloads.
[24:20] Diego: Yes. We'll compare no-cache, prefix-cache, and full-KV scenarios. Expect token-cost deltas in the report.
[24:45] Lena: Any concerns about data residency once fallback to hosted occurs? We don't want EU user data leaving the region.
[24:58] Rita: We can configure geo-fencing on routes so EU user traffic will not failover outside EU unless explicitly allowed; we'll mark that as a decision point in the pilot.
[25:20] Maya: That'll be in the options.
[25:40] [brief side chat about legal redlines]
[26:30] Priya: Please include redaction and PII-handling details for logs. We can't have raw PII in exported logs.
[26:40] Diego: We have built-in redaction hooks and configurable PII filters — will include config examples.
[27:05] Lena: Ok, let's outline the timeline: 1) Salesforce: sign pilot addendum; 2) Pilot kickoff week of 2027-09-13; 3) 72h bench during pilot; 4) finalize renewal by 2027-10-01. Is that realistic?
[27:30] Maya: Yes — that aligns with our renewals calendar.
[27:40] Tom: For the 72h bench, we need actionable metrics entry points to our APM. Can Diego add OTEL exporters?
[27:50] Diego: Yes, I'll add them and provide a dashboard link.
[28:10] [short pause, someone types]
[29:00] Maya: Anything else missing from the decision criteria?
[29:05] Lena: Make sure you include a rollback plan and the UX flags.
[29:12] Diego: We'll produce a rollback playbook, including traffic routing commands and runbook steps.
[29:22] Owen: We'll want a runbook with exact kubectl or CLI commands if it's on-prem.
[29:35] Diego: Noted.
[30:10] Maya: Alright, quick recap and owners — Diego will run the benchmark and share results; Maya will send renewal pricing and pilot addendum; Priya will confirm compliance docs; Tom will send traces and load profiles.
[30:30] Lena: Sounds good.
[31:00] Sofia: Procurement will review draft after Maya sends it.
[31:12] Maya: We'll aim to have the pricing doc in two business days.
[31:25] [32:00-46:00 detailed technical back-and-forth between Diego and Tom about batching, kernel selection, and KV cache configs — excerpted below]
[32:10] Diego: For kernels we pick optimized attention paths based on sequence length distribution — since your median is 120 tokens but tails go to 512 we will route long contexts to big nodes and short to quantized paths. This reduces cost by ~18% in similar customers.
[33:02] Tom: What about model variants — can we fall back to a 6-bit quantized version during bursts?
[33:12] Diego: Yes. We recommend a compatibility mapping; full-quality model for primary, 6-bit for burst with explicit telemetry. We'll include switching thresholds.
[34:00] Tom: Does switching require KV cache warm-up?
[34:06] Diego: There will be a cold-KV penalty; we'll run staged warm-ups before expected events.
[34:40] [murmurs]
[35:10] Lena: For the pilot what success thresholds do you need from Redwood's side?
[35:20] Maya: Demo a sustained 5k RPS with P95 <120ms for your prompt set, run SOC2 artifact review, and provide a clear renewal quote.
[35:38] Lena: Ok.
[36:00] [short pause for note-taking]
[36:40] Maya: Anything else?
[36:45] Priya: Can we get a naming convention for telemetry fields so our SIEM can ingest properly?
[36:52] Diego: We'll provide field mappings and sample logs.
[37:10] Sofia: One last ask from procurement: a single-page summary with line items for audit.
[37:20] Maya: We'll do that.
[38:00] [final 10 minutes recap]
[38:05] Maya: Recap — owners & deadlines: Maya: renewal pricing + pilot doc by 2027-09-03; Diego: bench results by 2027-09-06; Priya: compliance list by 2027-09-07; Tom: sample traces by 2027-09-02; schedule pilot kickoff week of 2027-09-13. Any objections?
[38:35] Lena: No objections.
[38:40] Tom: Fine.
[38:45] Maya: Great. We'll follow up with an email and links to the shared folder (pricing deck, benchmark plan, SOC2+ISO packet). Link placeholder: drive.redwood/avalon/pilot-pack.
[39:05] [closing salutations]
[39:12] Maya: Thanks everyone.
[39:15] Lena: Thanks.
[39:20] [call ends]
